text_cards.caption: ALL PASSANT
text_cards.description: A piece may capture an enemy piece on any square it moved through on the previous turn.
text_cards.quote: You never advance without losing something en passant, and you lose it because you're paying so much attention to the new thing. ---Ninette de Valois

text_cards.caption: BISHOP KNIGHT SWAP
text_cards.description: A \Bishop\ moves like a \Bishop, but captures only like a \Knight. A \Knight\ moves like a \Knight, but captures only like a \Bishop.
text_cards.quote: The human race has one really effective weapon, and that is laughter. ---Mark Twain

text_cards.caption: BRIBE
text_cards.description: On your turn you may perform an enemy pawn action instead. Draw an additional card.
text_cards.quote: Never underestimate the effectiveness of a straight cash bribe. ---Claud Cockburn

text_cards.caption: CAPTURE SWAP
text_cards.description: An X moves like an X, but captures only like a Y. A Y moves like a Y, but captures only like an X.
text_cards.quote: The human race has one really effective weapon, and that is laughter. ---Mark Twain

text_cards.caption: CAPTURE TWICE
text_cards.description: You may make two captures with two different pieces as one action.
text_cards.quote: As long as I breathe, I attack. ---Bernaud Hinault

text_cards.caption: CASTLES FOR EVERYONE
text_cards.description: \small Any \NoKing\ X may castle with a friendly \NoKing\ Y on the same rank or file. X jumps two squares towards (or over or onto) Y and Y moves to the square X jumped over.
text_cards.quote: I'm going to build castles from the rubble of your love. ---Freya Ridings

text_cards.caption: KING KNIGHT SWAP
text_cards.description: A \King\ acts only like a \Knight. A \Knight\ acts only like a \King.
text_cards.quote: The human race has one really effective weapon, and that is laughter. ---Mark Twain

text_cards.caption: QUEEN ROOK SWAP
text_cards.description: A \Queen\ moves like a \Queen, but captures only like a \Rook. A \Rook\ moves like a \Rook, but captures only like a \Queen.
text_cards.quote: The human race has one really effective weapon, and that is laughter. ---Mark Twain

text_cards.caption: TEN BY TEN
text_cards.description: The board is 10x10 and the pieces start in the central 8x8 squares. A \Pawn\ promotes on rank 9 (ranks numbered 1--10).
text_cards.quote: I don't have anything against walls. You know what it is? I like open spaces. ---Dion Dublin

text_cards.caption: MICRO-MANAGER
text_cards.description: A piece more than one rank ahead of the \King\ may not act.
text_cards.quote: \small I know it was your idea, but it was my idea to use your idea. --Anonymous

text_cards.caption: WAR AND PEACE
text_cards.description: You may make one move and one capture with two different pieces as one action. Castling is a \King\ move. Say when your turn is over.
text_cards.quote: Only the dead have seen the end of war. --Plato

text_cards.caption: KNIGHT SWAP
text_cards.description: Two friendly \NoKing\ pieces which are a knight move apart may swap places as an action.
text_cards.quote: Don't swap horses in crossing a stream. --Abraham Lincoln

text_cards.caption: TELEPORTER
text_cards.description: A \Bishop\ may move to any open square adjacent to a friendly pawn.
text_cards.quote: If I could teleport, I'd probably still be late. --Anonymous

text_cards.caption: SUMMONER
text_cards.description: A \Bishop\ may make a summoner action: move a friendly \NoKing\ to an adjacent square, or capture. A \Pawn\ may not be summoned to the first or last rank.
text_cards.quote: My name is Mortimer Alexander and I am a licensed summoner." "Darn. I'd hoped you were the pizza delivery guy. ---Jana Oliver

text_cards.caption: CYLINDER $\Rightarrow$
text_cards.description: The right and left side of the board are adjacent to each other. Pieces may not act left from their POV.
text_cards.quote: Always choose the right path and speak the truth. ---Mahatma Gandhi

text_cards.caption: TRADING PLACES
text_cards.description: You may swap the locations of a friendly \Knight\ and \Pawn\. This is a \Knight\ move.
text_cards.quote: You'll all be very, very sorry. ---Louis Winthorpe

text_cards.caption: COMPLICATE
text_cards.description: Deal two more cards.
text_cards.quote: When all else fails, complicate matters. ---Aaron Allston

text_cards.caption: FAST PAWNS
text_cards.description: A \Pawn\ may move any number of squares straight forward. En passant captures apply to entire path. A \Pawn may not move more than one square to the promotion rank. Draw another card.
text_cards.quote: In ceremonies of the horsemen, even the pawn must hold a grudge. ---Bob Dylan

text_cards.caption: LEND ME YOUR HORSE
text_cards.description: A non-pawn piece protected by a \Knight\ may also act like a \Knight.
text_cards.quote: "You should know better than to mount another's war-horse", I said with a smirk. ---Jessica Leake

text_cards.caption: POSSESSION
text_cards.description: A non-pawn piece protected by a \Knight\ may act like that \Knight\ (it is not the possessor). Kings cannot be possessed.
text_cards.quote: Possession is nine-tenths of the law. ---Anonymous

text_cards.caption: MOVE TWICE
text_cards.description: You may make two moves with two different pieces as one action. White may not use this card on move 1. Castling is a \King\ move.
text_cards.quote: When someone says you can't do something, do it twice and take pictures. ---Anonymous

text_cards.caption: CHECKERS
text_cards.description: A \Pawn\ moves and captures like a checkers man. Captures (including multiple) are forced. A \Pawn\ promotes as in chess, not as a checkers king.
text_cards.quote: These guys are playing checkers. I'm out here playing chess. When they figure it out, it's too late. ---Max Holloway

text_cards.caption: PRECOCIOUS PAWNS
text_cards.description: All pawns start advanced one rank. Draw another card.
text_cards.quote: Precocious was not the same as smart, much less the same as wise, and the perfect opposite of informed. ---Lionel Shriver

text_cards.caption: QUEEN KING KNIGHT
text_cards.description: A \Queen\ may only act like a \Knight\ or a \King.
text_cards.quote: The queen is the most powerful piece on the board --- if she is not distracted. ---Anonymous

text_cards.caption: CROWNED BISHOP
text_cards.description: A \Bishop\ may also act like a \King.
text_cards.quote: In the land of the blind the one-eyed man is king. ---Efren Ramirez

text_cards.caption: CROWNED ROOK
text_cards.description: A \Rook\ may also act like a \King.
text_cards.quote: In the land of the blind the one-eyed man is king. ---Efren Ramirez

text_cards.caption: REARGUARD
text_cards.description: After a \Queen\ move, a \Pawn\ may move to the empty square behind the queen as part of that move.
text_cards.quote: If you think you're going to be a backup, you're going to be a backup. ---Nick Foles

text_cards.caption: INSANE CYLINDER
text_cards.description: A piece may not move or capture backwards. The top and bottom of the board are edge-adjacent.
text_cards.quote: There's a fine line between genius and insanity. I have erased this line. ---Oscar Levant

text_cards.caption: CYLINDER
text_cards.description: The right and left sides of the board are edge-adjacent.
text_cards.quote: \tiny Everything in nature takes its form from the sphere, the cone and the cylinder. ---Paul Cezanne

text_cards.caption: MOVE SWAP
text_cards.description: A \NoKing\ X may swap places with a friendly \NoKing\ Y if X could move to Y's square.
text_cards.quote: Trading is very competitive and you have to be able to handle getting your butt kicked. ---Paul Tudor Jones

text_cards.caption: MOVE THROUGH FRIENDLY PIECES
text_cards.description: Friendly pieces do not block movement.
text_cards.quote: True friends stab you in the front. ---Oscar Wilde

text_cards.caption: ARCHBISHOP
text_cards.description: A \Queen\ may only act like a \Bishop\ or a \Knight.
text_cards.quote: If people want a sense of purpose they should get it from their archbishop. They should certainly not get it from their politicians. ---Harold MacMillan

text_cards.caption: CHANCELLOR
text_cards.description: A \Queen\ may only act like a \Rook\ or a \Knight.
text_cards.quote: When I'm stirring a saucepan, I don't say to myself, 'Now the chancellor is stirring a saucepan'. ---Angela Merkel

reference_cards.caption: ARC MATE RULES
reference_cards.description: Deal 1--2 rule cards in order; later cards stack. No check: at end of your turn, no king = you lose; opponent has no king = you win. One move or capture unless a card allows two (say ``done''). Pawns: not behind starting rank. ``+'' corner: draw another rule card.

reference_cards.caption: FISCHER RANDOM 960
reference_cards.description: Rank 1, files 1--8. \textbf{d8}: Queen on roll (light square). \textbf{d12} (twice): subtract 4s $\rightarrow$ 1--4 on dark empties; subtract 3s $\rightarrow$ 1--3 on light empties (swap if Q on dark). \textbf{d20} (twice): subtract 5s $\rightarrow$ 1--5; subtract 4s $\rightarrow$ 1--4. Last three: K on 2, R on 1 and 3. Example: 6, 9, 16 $\rightarrow$ B N R K R Q N B. Mirror Black.
